decision.reasoning: Both JCM1423 and1424 reference clarified rumen fluid266. JCM266 describes preheated rumen contents followed by centrifugation and supernatant collection. Different receiving doses (50 versus20ml) do not equate this product to whole rumen or an arbitrary filtered fluid. Combined-corpus validation exposed three existing MIM consumers of the changed rumen owner identifier. Three minimal guarded follow-on proposals maintain those existing links and explicitly preserve uncertainty in the legacy component assertions; they do not import or approve any additional source cases.
decision.applicability: The existing Clarified_rumen_fluid owner spans processed ruminal fluid. Its MICRO0000520 exact target requires cow origin, but primary DSMZ161/212 expressly allow cow OR sheep, while JCM266/355/1201 do not state an animal species. Reuse the existing processed-fluid owner with a local registry identity rather than create a duplicate or infer cow. This is a variable biological material, not an assertion that every source preparation has identical species or composition. JCM266 and DSMZ161 processing details remain distinct supplied forms; no unprocessed rumen-fluid equivalence is asserted. These three dependent-owner deltas are transactional prerequisites of this assigned source-owner correction, not scientific review of their underlying MicrobeDecoder observations.
